## The emulator remembers you now, and the "try it" link is findable

**Settings persist in the browser.** The emulator replayed the colour check and Squachy's whole walkthrough on every single page load, because persistence in the shim was opt-in through an environment variable and the WebAssembly build never set one — so every save was a no-op. It's backed by `localStorage` now, one key per NVS namespace, mirroring the one-file-per-namespace layout the desktop emulator uses.

`localStorage` rather than Emscripten's IDBFS on purpose: settings are written synchronously from inside every `put`, and `localStorage` is synchronous too, so the storage code keeps its exact shape. IDBFS is the more orthodox answer but `FS.syncfs` is async — it would need a debounce and a `visibilitychange` handler and would still lose the last write to a hard tab close.

Because first boot is genuinely worth seeing, there's a **Factory reset** button next to Reboot that clears it and replays the whole thing.

**The flasher has a "TRY IT NOW!" sunburst.** The emulator link previously existed only in the about text at the very bottom of the page, well past where most people stop reading. It's a badge in the header now, over on the right.

### The actually-useful part
- **Fixed**: the browser emulator forgot everything on reload — colour check and walkthrough replayed every visit
- **Added**: Factory reset in the emulator, since persistence otherwise makes first boot unreachable
- **Added**: "TRY IT NOW!" sunburst badge linking to the emulator from the top of the flasher page
